text:
maria: flagging a customer escalation from ACME-Corp — multiple p99 spikes and instances of gpu OOMs in us-east-1 since ~07:42 UTC. they report slow interactive assistants in production.
jon: saw their support thread. metrics show sudden KV cache cardinality growth on nodes serving redwood-xlarge-2; p99 up to 4.1s on /v1/chat.
li: pulled the node logs; allocator shows repeated cudaMalloc retries and a steady increase in small allocations. looks like kv shard count per model runner jumped from ~900 -> ~4200 in 10m.
sanjay: any pattern on request shape? long system messages or client-managed prefixes?
maria: ACME uses streaming + per-message metadata that includes a unique request id per turn — suspect that creates new kv keys every message, preventing reuse.
faq-bot: pro-tip: encourage clients to reuse conversation prefix keys and avoid including ephemeral GUIDs in cache keys.
jon: here's a snippet from /var/log/runtime on node-a12:
```
[2026-03-01T07:42:18Z] gpu_alloc: cudaMallocAsync(size=33554432) -> OOM, attempts=3
[2026-03-01T07:42:18Z] gpu_alloc: arena_free_count=0 arena_frag=72% arena_allocated=19.8GB
[2026-03-01T07:42:19Z] kv_cache: entries=4214 delta=+2800 in 8m
[2026-03-01T07:42:19Z] model-runner: request_id=acme-usr-xxx created kv_prefix=conv:acme:2026-03-01:7:42:...
```
li: allocator fragmentation high; defrag attempts are logged but freeable blocks=0. that suggests many small live allocations and the pool is fragmented.
sanjay: quick repro plan: simulate streaming clients that attach per-turn GUIDs and 200 concurrent sessions. i'll spin that up on perf-staging.
maria: mitigation options we should weigh now: 
  * immediate: apply per-tenant concurrent request cap (e.g., max-concurrency=40) via routing rules for ACME. non-invasive and reversible.
  * immediate: throttle streaming chunk size to reduce intermediate kv allocations and backpressure allocation rate. small change at gateway layer.
  * short-term: enable per-runtime kv-entry hard cap (e.g., 2500 entries) with LRU eviction; requires rolling restarts but should prevent unbounded growth.
  * risky: switch allocator from cudaMallocAsync to cudaMalloc fallback for this pool to see if fragmentation decreases; requires careful testing.
  * ops: drain and restart some processes to reclaim fragmentation (staggered), but operationally heavy.
jon: i've opened a temporary routing rule to drop ACME to 30% traffic on redwood-medium-1, they're sensitive to latency but can tolerate slightly lower quality for fallback. deploy-bot created canary.
deploy-bot: routing change initiated: route tenant-prefix acme-* -> redwood-medium-1 (canary 30% -> 100% over 5m).
li: perf-staging repro shows similar pattern: with 150 concurrent streaming sessions each sending 3 long turns, kv entries cross 3.5k in ~6m and p99 >3s; switching streaming chunk size to 512 bytes instead of 4k reduces allocation churn and p99 remains below 1.6s.
sanjay: trying per-tenant concurrency cap now for ACME in us-east-1 prod via runtime-routing; should be instant.
maria: support, please ping ACME with the temporary mitigation and recommend best-practices (reuse keys, remove ephemeral IDs).
support: pinged ACME; they acknowledged and asked about timeline. created ticket T-10021.
li: quick note on defrag: driver exposes cudaMemTrim on some versions; not reliable. our runtime logs show driver version 530.x — memTrim available but may require process-level call; defrag might not free cross-process fragmentation.
jon: because fragmentation won't recover until process restart, propose schedule: stagger restart 1/30 nodes every 60s in pool us-east-1-pool-A to avoid capacity loss. ops needed.
sanjay: doing controlled restarts now; will monitor p99.
jenkins-bot: rolling restart job started for pool us-east-1-pool-A (nodes=30, step=1).
oncall: please coordinate timing so we don't restart nodes serving other heavy tenants. tag @oncall for overlap windows.
maria: for postincident items: 
  - add per-tenant kv-rate metric and alert (entries/minute)
  - implement server-side dedup of ephemeral kv prefixes (strip GUID-like suffixes) as a safety net
  - add admin API to trim kv entries for a tenant (manual evict)
  - run allocator experiments in staging toggling cudaMallocAsync pool size and max arena and measure fragmentation regression
  - update docs and support playbook for large-context streaming (recommend chunk size, prefixes)
  - consider offering a 'large-context' dedicated SKU with bigger GPUs for these customers
li: also filing INF-901 (kv-rate telemetry), INF-902 (runtime-evict-admin-api), INF-903 (allocator-experiments).
sanjay: status after first 8 restarts: p99 dropped from 4.1s -> 1.5s and OOM logs stopped. kv entries gradually declined as evictions + restarts took effect.
maria: thanks team. leave thread with final state once stable 1hr. please paste any helpful dashboards or traces here for the postmortem.
support: dashboard links: https://grafana.redwood/boards/kv-growth?from=2225006600&to=2225007000 and ticket T-10021 updated with mitigation notes.
li: uploaded runtime traces: s3://redwood-traces/us-east-1/2225006789/trace.tar.gz
oncall: good job. we'll run the blameless postmortem and track infra changes.
